page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and features a cache configuration consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 154 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong single-core capabilities but limited multi-core and memory bandwidth throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated in the top 25%, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% and large block read/write bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU, the E4-2ads_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads that do not require dense parallel processing. It is suited for applications requiring large memory footprints but low CPU concurrency, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and single-threaded text processing. However, it is poorly suited for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, ray tracing, or high-throughput web serving, where its multi-core and database benchmarks rank in the bottom 10%.
